title: Home
body: BxRig BxRig brings an opinionated, beautiful and efficient desktop to Linux, built for developers. It turns a fresh CachyOS or Arch install into a finished developer rig: Hyprland with Noctalia (KDE Plasma stays installed beside it), BoxLang and MatchBox, your apps, your shell, your AI agents, all chosen in one guided setup. It is a single native program written in BoxLang and compiled with MatchB…

title: Command flags
body: Command flags Generated from docs/reference/cli.json . These flags work on every command: --json , --yes , --dry-run , --force , --quiet . title: Mice, trackpads and keyboards
body: Mice, trackpads and keyboards BxRig finds Apple Magic and Logitech devices and offers the helpers around them. Magic Mouse and Magic Trackpad work through the Linux kernel; Logitech's Logi Options+ has a Linux equivalent in Solaar. Detection needs no root and no extra tool: it reads the kernel's /sys/bus/hid/devices (vendor 05AC is Apple, 046D is Logitech; bus 0005 is Bluetooth, 0003 USB), bluetoo…

title: Scheduler
body: Scheduler BxRig runs its timed work on one scheduler: a BoxLang scheduler class on the BoxLang JVM, kept running by a user service. It runs the daily update check, your file backups, the BoxLang and module checks, and any task you add. Every run is recorded, so you can see what ran, how long it took and what failed. bxrig scheduler install --yes # once: the service, the built-in tasks, and the old…

title: Security
body: Security Releases are signed. CI signs each channel's version-latest.properties and install.sh with an Ed25519 key. The public key is built into the program and into the published installer. The installer and bxrig update verify the signature and the SHA-256 of every file they download; any mismatch stops before anything changes. The first curl | bash trusts the script it downloads (TLS and the bu…
